name: SubDL Scribe
description: SubDL Scribe brings SubDL.com to Jellyfin: it downloads missing subtitles for the languages and libraries you pick and uploads your own. Download is on by default; upload is off — enable at your choice. Requires a SubDL login and API Key plus a TMDb API Key.
overview: Sync subtitles with SubDL — download missing and upload new subtitles.

versions.changelog:
v12.1.12.158: Four credentials, no partial operation.
    The settings page enforced exactly one of the four credential fields: an empty TMDb
    key refused the save, while an empty SubDL email, password or API key saved happily
    and only surfaced later as a 404 from the login - and the page carried "Required"
    over all three sections, so the label and the behaviour disagreed.
    All four are now checked the same way and the empty one is named. They are not
    alternatives, which the documentation claimed ("username/password or API key"): the
    login pair authenticates the upload, the API key authenticates search, file download
    and the quota read, and the TMDb key resolves the ids in both directions. A run
    refuses to start without them, so the failure is one line at run start instead of a
    404 halfway through.
    Two switches existed for the ID gate and were read by no code path. They are removed
    rather than wired up: they claimed the gate was optional, and it is what makes the
    TMDb key load-bearing. With them go the branches that treated it as a flag.
    Loose .srt files beside a media file now go through language detection before an
    upload. A name without a language token used to be read as English on Jellyfin's
    convention, so a German subtitle was uploaded as English. Such a file is the sidecar
    counterpart of an 'und' stream now - same switch, same order (2 KB floor first),
    same outcomes: switch off, too little text or no language found all mean skip, and a
    detected language becomes the language. A sidecar whose language cannot be
    established no longer counts as covering anything, so the language is still fetched.
